messages:
mike: FYI a few customers reported quota spikes after clients upgraded to SDK 1.4.0. Looks like the route header rename is the culprit (X-Redwood-RouteId).

leah: We renamed to RouteId to reduce ambiguity. Did ingest/console expect the legacy header?

toni: Console still reads X-Redwood-Route. New header simply gets ignored so route->tenant mapping falls back to default.

priya: That explains misattribution. Quick plan: deploy a proxy shim that copies RouteId into Route, add Console acceptance for both, emit telemetry to track who only sends new header, and update SDK docs.

mike: Agreed. Edge shim is fastest. Template logic: if header present set legacy header to same value. No parsing.

edge-bot: deploy queued: edge/route-shim #142 -> staging at 1720010060 by mike

leah: Also add metric route.header.legacy_missing=true when only new header present so we can measure adoption per tenant.

toni: For SDKs, add runtime toggle `use_legacy_route_header` default true for one release, flip later. Add migration guide with examples for py/ts/go.

priya: Communication: release notes, support playbook, and give customers 7 days notice before removing shim. We'll keep shim for 14 days as safety.

mike: Staging smoke passed at 1720010180. Prod deploy in 5m. Monitor quota attribution for 3 hours after push.

leah: Follow-up: open RFC to canonicalize header handling (strip prefixes, lowercase, support both headers explicitly). Include tests across edge->ingest->console.

priya: I'll draft the docs and update the SDK changelogs. Thanks team.
